notes: Kamehameha I unified the major Hawaiian Islands, founded the Kingdom of Hawaii, and ruled until his death in 1819. Kauai and Niihau accepted his sovereignty in 1810, completing political unification without conquest.
Mehmed II, known as Mehmed the Conqueror, captured Constantinople in 1453, ended the Byzantine Empire, and transformed the Ottoman state into a major imperial power.
Constantine XI Palaiologos was the last Byzantine emperor. He reigned from 1449 and died during the Ottoman capture of Constantinople in 1453.
Pocatello was a leading chief of the Northwestern Shoshone in the mid-19th century, representing his people during conflict, displacement, and treaty negotiations with the United States.
Said bin Sultan ruled the Omani Empire from 1806 to 1856, expanded Omani influence across the western Indian Ocean, and made Zanzibar a principal political and commercial center of his empire.

Robert Guiscard ruled as Duke of Apulia and Calabria from 1059 to 1085, completed the Norman conquest of most of southern Italy, expelled the Byzantines after the capture of Bari, and led campaigns across the Adriatic.

Lady K'ab'al Xook was a principal queen of Yaxchilan and one of the best-documented royal women of the Classic Maya period. She is prominently depicted in major ceremonial monuments, including Lintel 24.
